messages:
deploy-bot: post-deploy smoke finished for release v2026.03.21-rc2. apac prefill probe shows p99=1.8s (baseline 0.6s), enqueued=high, errors 0.9%. tagging @oncall and #eng-releases. run: https://deploy.internal/runs/6245
rachel: noticed request spikes on prefill worker pool in apac2, looks like warmup produced burst of concurrent prefill jobs
marco: proxy tail shows `429` from prefill queue: `prefill-worker[apac2]: rate_limited enqueue`
devops: which flag controls prefill backpressure? iirc it's `prefill.window_size` and `prefill.rate_limit`
rachel: we shipped prefill.window_size=32 -> was 8 in prior release (commit a9b2f1)
marco: that explains the burst. increasing window increased enqueue parallelism, pushing kv cache warmups and saturating local workers
oncall: do we want immediate flipback or a pin of the region? impact currently limited to apac2, customers not reporting errors yet (observability only)
telemetry-bot: anomaly alert created: apac2_prefill_queue_depth > 3x baseline for 4m. alert-id: T-2026-APAC-33
devops: prefer flip flag first (runtime) then pin region to previous stable release while we validate behavior. lower blast radius
marco: agree. simple flip: `prefill.window_size=8` and `prefill.rate_limit=200/s` to match baseline
rachel: can we do a canary flip to one availability zone in apac2? if runtime supports per-az flag
devops: per-az flags are supported. i'll flip az-b first and watch queues for 5m
oncall: standby alert set. escalate to paging if errors >1% or p99 >1s
marco: az-b flipped to baseline. queue depth normalized in that AZ within 90s. p99 down to 0.65s
rachel: good signal. flip remaining AZs in apac2
telemetry-bot: updated alert: apac2_prefill_queue_depth returned to baseline across AZs. closing alert T-2026-APAC-33
devops: applied runtime change to all apac2 AZs and queued region pin: `pin-region apac2 to v2026.03.20-stable` (awaiting human approve)
marco: +1 for pin. keep rollout paused for apac and resume traffic shift after 20m stable window
rachel: documenting in release notes channel and linking postmortem stub: https://docs.internal/releases/2026-03-21-prefill-hotpatch
noncall: will monitor until 6123457989 (20m). if no regressions, we unpin and continue progressive rollout
devops: done — runtime flags reverted and infra pin recorded (change-id infra-802). leaving automated rollback job disabled for now
marco: followups: open a small revert PR for the prefill change (branch: revert/prefill-window-32) and add a synthetic test to catch prefill queue spikes
rachel: assigning PR to @marco, QA to @rachel. will add a smoke probe that asserts prefill queue < 1.5x baseline during warmup
oncall: thanks folks. stay on watch for the next 20m
